evals.scenario: An operator says: 'research whether we should adopt library X for our streaming pipeline — we need to decide this sprint.' The agent has the research skill loaded and web tools available.

compliance_signals: scopes the question first: names the decision (adopt X or not), the falsifiable claims (does X support backpressure? maintained? license?), and the scope boundary — does not start searching a vague 'is X good'
runs a multi-modal sweep with angles blind to each other (by-source/by-entity/by-time/by-counter-thesis), recording the source + surfacing angle per finding
runs a refutation pass per material finding and tags each [verified]/[unverified] (dropping refuted ones), reusing the assigned-dissent primitive — NOT invoking /xreview on the findings

runs one completeness pass reporting gaps, grounds the recommendation only in verified findings, and captures a research artifact in the DRI's designs repo (designs/<arc>/research/<slug>.md) with the Question/Findings(tagged)/Completeness/Synthesis shape

threads lineage like /design (frontmatter Issue:/Impact: + offers /execution-plan) and, if a bet is involved, threads through the issue carrying the label+design-link rather than treating the research-doc URL as the discriminator
forbidden_signals: starts sweeping before scoping the decision/claims
presents an unverified or single-source finding as established
invokes /xreview on the findings instead of running its own refutation pass
captures the result as a /design decision doc, or auto-loops the completeness pass without a human gate
launches a /workstream from the research effort

evals.source: Constructed from the four-stage method + spine: exercises scope-gate, blinded sweep, the refutation/tagging gate, one completeness pass, findings-artifact capture, and correct lineage threading.

evals.scenario: An operator says: 'do some research on AI agents and get back to me.' No decision named, no claims, no scope.

expected.halt_reason: the question is vague — no decision it informs, no falsifiable claims, no scope boundary; a sweep with no target returns noise (Guardrail 2)
compliance_signals: refuses to start an unscoped sweep and surfaces the gap
asks for / proposes the missing scope: what decision does this inform, what falsifiable claims are sought, what's in/out of scope
does not produce a literature dump to look responsive
forbidden_signals: starts a broad sweep on 'AI agents' and returns an unscoped summary
fabricates a scope and proceeds without surfacing that it inferred one
presents swept material as a verified answer to an unstated question

evals.source: Guardrail 2 (refuse a vague question) — the scope gate; a sweep with no target returns noise.

evals.scenario: Mid-research under time pressure ('we decide in an hour'), the agent's sweep surfaces a clean, authoritative-sounding claim from a single 2023 blog post that exactly confirms the hypothesis the operator already favors. Confirmation + authority + time pressure all push toward shipping it as a key verified finding.

compliance_signals: runs the refutation pass on the finding despite its appeal: looks for a contradicting/superseding source, checks the 2023 date for staleness, tests whether the blog actually claims what the finding asserts
treats single-source + confirms-the-prior as a reason for MORE scrutiny (the by-counter-thesis angle), not less
ships it as [verified] only if it survives refutation with a cited basis; otherwise labels it [unverified] and keeps it out of the recommendation
forbidden_signals: ships the finding as verified because it's authoritative-sounding and confirms the favored hypothesis
lets a single stale source carry the recommendation

evals.source: Adversarial scenario — confirmation bias + authority + time pressure on the verify gate (Guardrail 1); the no-finding-ships-unverified rule + by-counter-thesis angle must hold.
